claims.text: Pre-travel visit assesses, communicates and manages risk
claims.quote: healthcare professionals can conduct a risk assessment for each traveler, communicate risk by sharing information about potential health hazards, and manage risk by various means.

claims.text: Specialist consultation indicated for all international travelers, particularly complicated history, pregnancy, special risks, long itineraries
claims.quote: a comprehensive consultation with a travel medicine specialist is indicated for all international travelers and is particularly important for those with a complicated health history, pregnant women, anyone taking special risks

claims.text: Visit covers health background, itinerary, duration, purpose, activities
claims.quote: Effective pre-travel consultations require attention to the traveler's health background and incorporate the itinerary, trip duration, travel purpose, and activities planned during travel

claims.text: No physical exam; separate appointment may be needed for fitness to travel
claims.quote: The typical pre-travel consultation does not include a physical examination, and a separate appointment with the same or a different healthcare professional might be necessary to assess fitness for travel.

claims.text: Everyday risks listed
claims.quote: reminding the traveler of ubiquitous risks (e.g., injury, foodborne and waterborne infections, vector-borne diseases, respiratory tract infections, blood-borne infections, and sexually transmitted infections)

claims.text: Vaccine need depends on purpose, season, duration, destination; update routine vaccines
claims.quote: The purpose of travel, season, duration, and specific destination within a country will inform the need for vaccines. At the same time, the pre-travel consultation presents an opportunity to update routine vaccines

claims.text: Flu vaccine for all travelers
claims.quote: Current-season vaccine is recommended for all travelers.

claims.text: MMR for travelers without documented immunity
claims.quote: Vaccination is recommended for all international travelers ≥6 months old without documented immunity.

claims.text: Hepatitis A among most common vaccine-preventable travel diseases
claims.quote: Hepatitis A is one of the most common vaccine-preventable diseases acquired during travel.

claims.text: Typhoid highest risk South Asia
claims.quote: The highest risk is for travelers going to South Asia (e.g., Bangladesh, Pakistan, and India)

claims.text: Yellow fever risk areas and entry proof
claims.quote: Risk occurs in defined areas of Sub-Saharan Africa and the Amazonian regions of South America. Some countries require proof of vaccination for entry.

claims.text: Malaria counseling topics
claims.quote: discuss malaria transmission, ways to reduce risk, including mosquito-bite avoidance, recommendations for prophylaxis, symptoms of malaria, and the need for prompt medical care if symptoms develop.

claims.text: Self-treatable conditions include altitude illness, motion sickness, travelers' diarrhea
claims.quote: Altitude illness - HIV exposure (occupational) - Jet lag - Malaria - Motion sickness - Travelers' diarrhea

claims.text: Travelers' diarrhea self-management and when to seek care (24-36 hours, high fever, dehydration, bloody diarrhea)
claims.quote: most symptoms can be managed with fluid replacement plus loperamide or bismuth subsalicylate; consider prescribing travelers antibiotics they can carry with them for use in the event of incapacitating diarrhea

claims.text: Seek care at 24-36 hours, high fever, dehydration, bloody diarrhea
claims.quote: tell them to seek medical attention if symptoms persist for 24–36 hours or are particularly severe, such as high fevers, dehydration, or bloody diarrhea.

claims.text: Bring quality drugs; counterfeit drugs abroad
claims.quote: the increasing awareness of substandard and counterfeit drugs in pharmacies in certain countries makes it important for travelers to bring quality manufactured drugs with them from a reliable supplier.

claims.text: Medication interaction review
claims.quote: review each traveler's medication list for possible drug-drug interactions

claims.text: Travel medical insurance
claims.quote: Instruct travelers on how to obtain travel medical insurance

claims.text: Carry-on, original bottles, prescription copies
claims.quote: keep medications and supplies in carry-on luggage, to keep medications in their original prescription bottles, and to carry copies of their written prescriptions.

claims.text: What to bring: Box 1.1.1 itinerary items
claims.quote: Countries and specific regions, including order of countries, if >1 country, and layovers - Outbreaks at destination - Rural or urban destinations

claims.text: What to bring: medications, allergies, pregnancy, breastfeeding, immunization history (Box 1.1.1 headings)
claims.quote: Immunization History_** - Routine vaccines - Travel vaccines

claims.text: Activities examples: diving, high-elevation, animal contact
claims.quote: Animal interactions (including visiting farms, touring live animal markets)

claims.text: VFR travelers at higher typhoid risk, may skip pre-travel care
claims.quote: Travelers visiting friends and relatives are at increased risk because they might be less careful with food and water while abroad than other travelers and might not seek pre-travel health consultation or typhoid vaccination.

claims.text: Vaccine recommended 2 years and older to risk areas
claims.quote: Typhoid vaccine is recommended for travelers 2 years and older going to areas where risk for exposure to Typhi is recognized.

claims.text: Fecal-oral spread via food or water
claims.quote: Typhoid and paratyphoid fever are acquired through consumption of water or food contaminated by feces of an acutely infected or convalescent person, or a person with chronic, asymptomatic carriage.

claims.text: 85% of US cases in travelers, more than 70% from South Asia
claims.quote: Approximately 85% of typhoid fever and 80% of paratyphoid fever cases in the United States occur among international travelers; of those, more than 70% are in travelers returning from South Asia

claims.text: Trips under 1 week
claims.quote: travelers have acquired typhoid fever during visits of <1 week to countries where the disease is highly endemic (e.g., Bangladesh, India, Pakistan).

claims.text: Map: Mexico shaded; most of North America and Europe unshaded
claims.quote: Most countries in North America (except Mexico), most of Europe, and some island nations in the Pacific remain unshaded, meaning the typhoid vaccine is not recommended.

claims.text: Two licensed US vaccines (Typhim Vi IM, Vivotif oral)
claims.quote: Two typhoid vaccines are licensed for use in the United States: Vi capsular polysaccharide vaccine (ViCPS) (Typhim Vi, manufactured by Sanofi Pasteur) for intramuscular use; and live attenuated vaccine (Vivotif

claims.text: Both protect 50% to 80%
claims.quote: Because these vaccines protect 50–80% of recipients, remind travelers that typhoid immunization is not 100% effective

claims.text: Table: ViCPS age 2+, 0.5 mL IM, booster every 2 years
claims.quote: Booster | ≥2 years | 0.5 mL, IM injection | 1 | N/A | Every 2 years

claims.text: Table: Ty21a age 6+, 4 capsules every other day, booster every 5 years
claims.quote: Booster | ≥6 years | 1 capsule, orally every other day2 | 4 | 48 hours | Every 5 years

claims.text: ViCPS at least 2 weeks before travel
claims.quote: Primary vaccination with ViCPS consists of one 0.5 mL (25 µg) dose administered intramuscularly ≥2 weeks before travel.

claims.text: Ty21a: refrigerate not frozen, all 4 doses, swallow whole, cool liquid no warmer than 98.6F, 1 hour before and 2 hours after meal
claims.quote: The capsules should be kept refrigerated (not frozen), and all four doses must be taken to achieve maximum efficacy. Each capsule should be swallowed whole (not chewed) and taken with cool liquid no warmer than 37°C (98.6°F)

claims.text: Meal timing
claims.quote: approximately 1 hour before a meal and ≥2 hours after a previous meal.

claims.text: Alcohol 1 hour before to 2 hours after
claims.quote: avoiding alcohol consumption 1 hour before and 2 hours after administration, because alcohol can disintegrate the enteric coating.

claims.text: Finish at least 1 week before exposure; missed dose undefined
claims.quote: Travelers should complete the Ty21a vaccine regimen ≥1 week before potential exposure. The approach for addressing a missed oral vaccine dose or taking a dose late is undefined.

claims.text: Some think 1 day late may not matter; no studies
claims.quote: Some suggest that minor deviations in the dosing schedule (e.g., taking a dose 1 day late) might not alter vaccine efficacy; no studies have shown the effect of such deviations, however.

claims.text: Incomplete course may not give full protection
claims.quote: If travelers do not complete four doses as directed, they might not achieve an optimal immune response.

claims.text: Side effects of each vaccine
claims.quote: Adverse reactions most often associated with ViCPS vaccine include headache, injection-site reactions, fever, and general discomfort. Adverse reactions to Ty21a vaccine are rare and mainly consist of abdominal discomfort, diarrhea, fever, headache, nausea, vomiting, and rash.

claims.text: Contraindications: fever, gastroenteritis
claims.quote: Neither the ViCPS nor the Ty21a vaccine should be given to people with an acute febrile illness; in addition, Ty21a is not recommended for use in people with acute gastroenteritis.

claims.text: Live vaccine not in pregnancy or immunocompromised including HIV
claims.quote: Live vaccines, including Ty21a vaccine, should not be given to pregnant women or immunocompromised people, including those with HIV.

claims.text: ViCPS can be considered in pregnancy when benefits outweigh risks
claims.quote: consider ViCPS for pregnant women when the benefits of vaccination outweigh potential risks (e.g., when the likelihood of exposure to Typhi is high).

claims.text: ViCPS theoretically safer for immunocompromised
claims.quote: The intramuscular vaccine (ViCPS) presents a theoretically safer alternative than the live, oral vaccine (Ty21a) for immunocompromised travelers.

claims.text: Household contacts; no secondary transmission
claims.quote: The Ty21a vaccine can be administered to household contacts of immunocompromised people; although vaccine organisms can be shed transiently in the stool of vaccine recipients, secondary transmission of vaccine organisms has not been documented.

claims.text: ViCPS only contraindication prior severe reaction
claims.quote: The only contraindication to vaccination with ViCPS vaccine is a history of severe local or systemic reactions after a previous dose.

claims.text: Antibiotics 72 hours before and after
claims.quote: Vaccination with the Ty21a vaccine should be delayed for >72 hours after the administration of any antimicrobial agent, and antibiotics should not be given to a patient ≤72 hours after the last dose of the Ty21a vaccine.

claims.text: Atovaquone-proguanil only 10 or more days after last dose; mefloquine and chloroquine OK
claims.quote: atovaquone-proguanil should be administered only if 10 days or more have elapsed since the final dose of Vivotif was ingested; mefloquine and chloroquine can be administered together with the Ty21a vaccine.

claims.text: Live virus vaccines any interval
claims.quote: Ty21a vaccine can be administered simultaneously or at any interval before or after live virus vaccines (e.g., measles-mumps-rubella, oral polio, or yellow fever vaccines).

claims.text: Large inoculum; food and water precautions after vaccination
claims.quote: a large bacterial inoculum can overwhelm vaccine-induced immunity. Therefore, vaccinated travelers should follow recommended food and water precautions

claims.text: No paratyphoid vaccine
claims.quote: No vaccines are available for paratyphoid fever

claims.text: Incubation 6-30 days; fever to 102-104F by day 3 or 4
claims.quote: The typical incubation period for typhoid fever is 6–30 days

claims.text: Fever pattern
claims.quote: a fever that increases daily from low-grade to 39–40°C (approximately 102–104°F) by the third or fourth day of illness.

claims.text: Complications in 10% to 15% of hospitalized patients: hemorrhage, perforation
claims.quote: Serious complications of typhoid fever occur in 10–15% of hospitalized patients, generally after 2–3 weeks of illness, and include life-threatening gastrointestinal hemorrhage, intestinal perforation, and encephalopathy.

claims.text: Blood culture is preferred diagnosis (in-person testing)
claims.quote: blood culture is therefore the preferred method of diagnosis.

claims.text: Never too late
claims.quote: It is never too late for a pre-travel consultation.

claims.text: Last-minute defined as within 2 weeks
claims.quote: the last-minute traveler (LMT) is anyone departing for an international destination on short notice, typically ≤2 weeks.

claims.text: Full assessment, vaccines as time permits, focused counseling; telemedicine
claims.quote: clinics can offer dedicated hours or telemedicine services. Even with very limited time, every LMT should receive a full pre-travel assessment, all indicated vaccinations as time permits, and focused counseling

claims.text: Imminent travel: telehealth or secure messaging
claims.quote: If travel is imminent, healthcare professionals can still provide telehealth or secure digital messaging for prevention counseling

claims.text: Immunocompromised: 3 to 4 months ahead
claims.quote: For LMTs who are immunocompromised, timing of vaccination requires special consideration, and they should seek pre-travel services 3 to 4 months before their trip.

claims.text: Injectable typhoid among single-dose vaccines for LMTs
claims.quote: research supports the use of certain single-dose vaccines, if indicated, to initiate protection in LMTs. These include - Hepatitis A (monovalent) - Influenza - Meningococcal (quadrivalent, ACWY) - Polio booster (inactivated) - Typhoid (injectable)

claims.text: YF certificate valid 10 days after
claims.quote: Documentation of vaccination against YF on the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP) becomes valid 10 days after administration.

claims.text: Multiple doses: see provider as soon as possible
claims.quote: Because some vaccines require multiple doses, it’s best to see your health care provider as soon as possible.

claims.text: Check destination page
claims.quote: Check CDC’s webpage for your destination to see what vaccines or medicines you may need

claims.text: Yellow fever only at authorized center
claims.quote: If yellow fever vaccine is recommended or required for your destination, you’ll need to go to a vaccine center authorized to give yellow fever vaccinations.

claims.text: Possible travel vaccines list includes cholera, JE, meningococcal, polio, rabies
claims.quote: Japanese encephalitis - MMR (Measles, Mumps, Rubella) - Meningococcal - Monkeypox - Pneumococcal - Polio - Rabies

claims.text: XDR Pakistan

claims.text: Handwashing and 60% sanitizer
claims.quote: Use hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol if soap and water are not available.

claims.text: Water and ice

claims.text: Hot food, unpeelable produce, street vendors

claims.text: Street vendors
claims.quote: Avoid food and drinks from street vendors unless they are steaming hot when served.

claims.text: Fever: see a doctor, tell where and when
claims.quote: See a doctor if you have a fever and feel very ill. Tell the doctor where and when you traveled.

claims.text: Vaccines do not protect against paratyphoid
claims.quote: Available vaccines do not protect against paratyphoid fever.
